text:
Alex (AE): FYI customer's procurement just surfaced a blocker: their AP won't pay AWS Marketplace invoices because the vendor on the invoice is AWS, not Redwood. POC needs to start Monday. Can we move quickly?
Maria - Finance: That's common. AWS bills on their own invoices; we can't swap the biller name. What specifically does their AP require on the invoice to approve payment? vendor name, remit address, tax id?
Katy Procurement: They need vendor name + remit-to address and a matching PO number. Their ERP validates supplier name against their vendor master. If the invoice doesn't match, it's flagged. They *prefer* marketplace purchases but will accept a direct supplier invoice if legal/finance approves.
Alex (AE): Buyer insists they must have a marketplace transaction for compliance, but also insists the invoice show Redwood. Contradiction.
Jordan - Deals: Two practical options: 1) One-off direct Redwood invoice for the POC at marketplace-equivalent pricing (fastest), 2) Try to force a marketplace flow and then issue a Redwood self-bill or credit to reconcile (slower, needs legal). Which path do we want?
Maria - Finance: Option 2 requires legal review and a credit memo workflow; payment timing will likely slip. Option 1 is doable for small POCs. Finance can approve direct invoicing for single-cycle POCs under $10k if Deal Desk signs off.
Sarah - Deal Desk: Confirmed. We can approve a one-off quote at marketplace-equivalent price for POCs under $10k without exec approval. It must be explicitly non-binding and exclude commit discounts. Need a quote amount and Net30 terms.
Katy Procurement: If we go direct, I will ask buyer's AP to accept our supplier paperwork (W9 + vendor form) and a PO that matches the Redwood invoice. That should clear their ERP match rules. If they *must* have a marketplace record, they sometimes do a token marketplace card purchase + Redwood invoice for the actual service.
Alex (AE): POC estimate is $7,500. Customer prefers marketplace-only purchases but is open to the token marketplace purchase if it helps.
Maria - Finance: I'll create supplier profile docs and attach to ticket. Note: doing a token marketplace purchase can create accounting confusion; we'll need to ensure we don't double-recognize revenue. Finance will treat the token as separate; the POC will be direct revenue.
billing-bot: Created FIN-2026-89: evaluate marketplace remittance workaround and token purchase pattern. Assigned: maria.finance.
Jordan - Deals: Recommend we offer: direct Redwood invoice for POC (Net30), mirror marketplace list price, include supplier paperwork for AP, and suggest buyer do a $50 marketplace token purchase if their internal compliance requires a marketplace trace. That keeps commit tracking intact for later conversion.
Sarah - Deal Desk: I'll draft the quote: itemized single-line POC $7,500, Net30, one-time, non-binding. No commit discounts, no marketplace SKUs referenced. Uploading to SFDC now.
Katy Procurement: Please include our Redwood vendor form in the SFDC attachment so I can forward to buyer's AP quickly. Also include contact for finance to expedite vendor-add if needed.
Alex (AE): I'll message buyer: propose direct invoice + optional $50 marketplace token if they insist, and offer supplier paperwork. Will ask for PO to include on our invoice.
Maria - Finance: If buyer insists strictly on marketplace for payment routing, escalate to legal. We can do a credit/offset later but that slows cash collection. For speed, direct invoice is the path of least resistance.
Jordan - Deals: Also flag CRM: mark this POC as 'marketplace-equivalent' so later commit conversion applies same pricing and we avoid accidental commit discounts before contract signature.
Alex (AE): Great. I'll confirm with buyer and loop in procurement contact. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Sarah - Deal Desk: Quote uploaded. If finance/legal need to review the vendor paperwork before invoicing, ping me and I'll hold the quote until cleared.
Maria - Finance: Uploaded W9 + vendor profile to FIN-2026-89. If AP refuses to accept vendor form alongside AWS invoice, we will proceed with direct invoice and request PO that matches Redwood remit.
Katy Procurement: Following up with buyer's AP now; will report back within the hour.
Alex (AE): Closing loop for now. I'll post update when buyer confirms preference.
